name: Flameleaf Sumac

facts.how: Cold-steep for sumac-ade; dry and grind for the spice
facts.where: Fence rows and rocky hillsides; scarlet fall foliage

caution: Cashew family: those with strong cashew or mango allergies should be careful. Poison sumac has WHITE berries and lives in swamps, not on Texas hillsides; red upright clusters are the safe signature.

sections.title: Harvesting
sections.body: Snip whole red cones on a dry day and taste first: rain washes the tang off, and it returns after a few dry days. Sour is what you want.

sections.title: Sumac-ade
sections.body: Swish clusters in cold water until it turns pink lemonade, strain through cloth, sweeten. Heat turns it bitter, so keep it cold.
